subject: HIGHEST-ALGEBRAIC function
notes: OVERTURNED PARTIAL → NOT-IMPLEMENTED, same two grounds as rule 2. (1) EDITIONS: `ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY` (§11.9.5/§8.8.1.4) and the §3.167 standard decimal floating-point usages (float-decimal-16, float-decimal-34 — USAGE per §13.18.60.4 GR17/GR18) are both COBOL-2014 additions; the rule as worded does not exist at COBOL-2002. (2) VERDICT: no code implements this rule anywhere — the prohibited combination is doubly unreachable through two INDEPENDENT non-supports that have nothing to do with §15.43, so nothing has ever evaluated the rule's condition. Both non-supports are conformance-legal and I re-derived them rather than inheriting them: DataBinder rejects STANDARD-BINARY with COBOL0806, and Annex A.3 item 2 reads 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (NOTE 1 adds that the mode is obsolete); FLOAT-DECIMAL-16/34 are rejected at ParseUsage with COBOL1564 under A.3 item 19. Worth recording for whoever revisits this: A.3 item 3 makes ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-DECIMAL processor-dependent TOO, so WiseOwl COBOL's support for it is a choice, not an obligation — which is why rule 2's combination is writable and rule 3's is not. Vacuous truth is not implementation: if either half is ever supported, nothing enforces this. No spec-derived test, and none constructible. || DERIVED VERDICT from the ONE owner determination (kb/Work PB198; owner protocol 2026-08-30, survey unanimous): ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY IS DECLINED, so a rule conditioned SOLELY on that mode is unreachable and its verdict follows mechanically rather than being adjudicated row by row. THE GROUND IS PROCESSOR-DEPENDENCE, NOT OBSOLESCENCE. Annex A.3 item 2: 'The ARITHMETIC IS STANDARD-BINARY clause in the OPTIONS paragraph is dependent on the capabilities of the processor' (cite.py --check A.3 -> OK, item 2), and §4.2.6 gives the implementor the discretion not to claim support, plus the duty to warn at compile time and to document the absence ('The absence of processor-dependent elements from an implementation shall be specified in the implementor's user documentation' -> --check OK). Obsolescence grants NOTHING here: Annex F.2's own preamble says 'A conforming implementation shall support obsolete language elements EXCEPT for elements that are also optional or processor-dependent' (--check -> OK), so it is the processor-dependence that licenses the decline and the obsolescence is merely corroborating. REVISITABLE, by the standard's own words: F.2 item 3 ('STANDARD-BINARY arithmetic and STANDARD BINARY Intermediate Data Item. These features have not been implemented as of the writing of this revision by any COBOL provider.' -> --check OK) adds 'Unlike other obsolete features, it is intended that interest in these facilities will be reevaluated during the next revision of standard COBOL and before any final decision is made on whether or not to remove them from the next revision' (--check -> OK). THE SCREEN, MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE SET: the decline moved from DataBinder to OptionsBinder.ArithmeticOf, the single point every unit kind's OPTIONS clause is read through - DataBinder never saw a METHOD's or an INTERFACE's paragraph, so those two arms drew NO diagnostic at all at --std 2014 (kb/Work PB197). All seven unit kinds now draw exactly one COBOL0806, and ArithmeticModeScreenDriftTests reads the options-bearing productions OUT OF THE GRAMMAR so a new one cannot be added unscreened. Per-edition diagnostics are pinned with their ABSENCES too: 2002 -> 0900 + 0806, 2014 -> 0806 alone, 2023 -> 0806 + 0903. SELECTION IS DERIVED, NOT LISTED: inventory-schema.json's derived-verdicts.standard-binary-only carries the predicate as DATA, read by both the batch generator and the C# drift test, and the drift test holds every selected row at this verdict so the population cannot drift back into the four states it carried before (NOT-IMPLEMENTED 3, blank 2, NEEDS-OWNER-DECISION 4, CONFORMS 1).
